gap: No result ChatGPT got states how loud each amp's moving-coil phono input can play a low-output cartridge. With a 0.25 mV MC cartridge at full volume, the Marantz MODEL 30 reaches its full 100 W, the Luxman L-505Z about 69 W and the Musical Fidelity A1 only about 7.7 W. The Rega Elex Mk4 has no MC input at all.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Luxman L-505Z page (luxman.com) and the cited What Hi-Fi best-buys page. The Luxman page gives raw input sensitivities (MM 2.5 mV, MC 0.3 mV) but never turns them into gain or watts for a given cartridge. The What Hi-Fi page returned only its headline when fetched, so I could not check its text. The cited Rhythm Audio/Darko and Stereophile Recommended Components pages were not opened within the tool budget. ChatGPT's answer lists all five amps as plain 'MM/MC' or 'MM' with no gain figures. Because the Luxman page already has the raw inputs, this is a new derivation rather than a new fact, so it scores 2 and not 3.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's 'best for moving-coil' label for the Marantz MODEL 30: it has the most MC gain of the sourced amps (≈101 dB to the speaker terminals), three MC load settings (33/100/390 Ω) and about 30 dB of overload headroom on both MM and MC. It also shows that the Musical Fidelity A1's 'MM/MC' label is misleading for low-output MC owners. A 0.25 mV cartridge gets only about 7.7 W from it at full volume, so those owners should buy the Marantz or the Luxman, or add a step-up transformer or external phono stage. The Rega Elex Mk4 needs an external stage for any MC cartridge.
